That

exemption covers the roof covering only. On commercial buildings, condominiums, townhouses, and other attached or multi-family structures, the same code treats roofing as ordinary maintenance up to 25 percent of the roof area in a 12-month period; work beyond that threshold requires a permit. Structural work — cutting or replacing load-bearing framing or altering the roof structure — always requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(b), regardless of building type.

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: In New Jersey it is that permit line: roofing work beyond 25% of the roof area in 12 months on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building needs a permit. Roofers also use a 25% rule of thumb for repair versus replacement: once damage covers more than about a quarter of a roof, a full replacement usually costs less over time than continued repairs. In practice, structural repairs always require a local construction permit, and roof replacements generally require one too, except a covering-only reroof on a detached one- or two-family home.

When a permit applies, New Jersey's Rehabilitation Subcode (N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4) calls for full removal of the existing covering, with no recover-over, when the roof is water-soaked or deteriorated, when the covering is wood shake, slate, clay, cement, or asbestos-cement tile, or when two or more layers already exist, so a third layer of asphalt shingles is not allowed.

sections.heading: Why Belleville Homeowners Choose Newark Quality Roofing

c.v: How do I find a reliable roofing contractor?

runs.v: The best way is to start with registration: home improvement contractors must register with the New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs, and New Jersey requires a written contract for home improvement work over $500. State registration requires commercial general liability insurance, and New Jersey law requires workers' compensation insurance for contractors with employees, so ask each roofing company for proof of both. Confirm a valid physical address and phone number, check local references and reviews, and request multiple detailed written estimates from roofing contractors for the same scope. Local contractors are typically more familiar with New Jersey's specific weather challenges.

It is also important to ask what the warranty covers. Warranties should cover both the manufacturer's materials and the contractor's workmanship; workmanship warranties can last up to 25 years depending on the contractor, and a limited lifetime warranty can cover both materials and labor. GAF-certified contractors can offer enhanced warranties such as System Plus, while the GAF Golden Pledge Limited Warranty, which includes a 50-year material warranty, comes only through GAF's top Master Elite tier, so ask any roofer which tier it holds. Roofing warranties provide long-term protection for homeowners when every term is in writing.

Newark Quality Roofing meets that checklist with registration, liability insurance, GAF-certified installation, and more than 25 years of experience. Our commitment shows in the details you can check: crews equipped for both pitched and flat roofs, a focus on the flashing where most leaks start, photographs of the damage and the finished work, a written workmanship warranty on labor, and a magnet sweep for nails at cleanup. Excellence in roofing is that record, and we keep it for every job to ensure the owner knows exactly what was done.
